question: Does a STATE survive as a predictive object once it is given a lifecycle (dwell/hysteresis), and does an EVENT target beat it? Or is neither predictable from price geometry alone?

carried_from_phase1.root_cause: frozen MARKET_BEHAVIOR is a memoryless per-bar classifier: churn 0.6292@M15/0.6194@H1 on 20 months, duration median 1 bar at all timeframes, surrogate churn 0.62 ~ observed => churn is definitional, not market structure
carried_from_phase1.implication: any target derived from the frozen per-bar label inherits memorylessness; a stateful redefinition must be tested explicitly

feature_rule: features are PURE OHLC-derived indicators (atr_pctl, er10, slope5, rng_exp, vel4, acc, eff3, act3). Labeler outputs are STRICTLY EXCLUDED from features to avoid circularity.

targets.T2_STATEFUL_STATE: hysteresis(k=2) applied to the frozen label sequence, then t -> t+8
targets.T4_EVENT_BREAKOUT: causal event: within t+1..t+8, close beyond the prior 96-bar range {UP_BREAK, DOWN_BREAK, NONE}

protocol.model: multinomial logistic regression, C=1.0, lbfgs, deterministic; NO complexity change across targets
protocol.walk_forward: expanding, 5 folds covering the last 40% of bars
protocol.primary_metric: out-of-sample log-loss gain in bits vs unconditional class-prior baseline (DeltaLL)
protocol.null: block-shuffled target (block=48), full protocol re-run, NPERM=30, empirical p = share(null DeltaLL >= observed)
protocol.acceptance: a target SURVIVES only if DeltaLL >= effect_floor AND empirical p <= 0.05 AND it beats the persistence baseline accuracy

decision_rules.NEITHER: all targets fail => price geometry alone does not support state/event prediction at this sample
decision_rules.no_tuning: no threshold change; k=2 chosen a priori from Phase 1 (k=2 gave churn 0.1507)
